milestones.title: Stage 0 - Reproducible reference
milestones.description: FP32 reference and the pinned OPT ReLU positive control pass original numerical gates. Torch 2.12 preserves the BF16 permutation failure; canonical down remains a costly diagnostic. Practical BF16 grouped execution and its cost evidence remain open.

milestones.title: Stage 1 - Hindsight sparsity envelope
milestones.description: Measure individual-neuron, per-layer, and joint omission quality on whole-document and domain splits. Exit requires useful sparsity on unseen modern-model inputs under predeclared quality criteria.

milestones.title: Stage 2 - Physical packing and cache traces
milestones.description: Completed v0.4 development trace study: 72 conditions and four cache budgets. One grouped condition passes the prospective aggregate-PPL and simulated-traffic screen; strongest warm saving is 15.54%. Held-out quality and physical transfer/runtime gates remain open.

milestones.title: Stage 3 - Causal working-set prediction
milestones.description: First causal experiment completed in v0.7: all four selectors fail quality; three also fail affordability. No nominee for runtime/refinement. Broader quality/bytes/cost curves and useful predictor feasibility remain open; preserve the frozen negative result.

milestones.title: Stage 4 - Bounded RAM-to-VRAM execution
milestones.description: Implement bounded GPU slots and staging with actual skipped reads/computation. Compare against strongest same-budget streaming, cache, and CPU/GPU baselines after charging every overhead. Still gated after v0.7: no causal selector passes the frozen development screen.

milestones.title: Stage 5 - Corrective refinement
milestones.description: Define unsafe omission, detect it cheaply, add omitted contributions before downstream commitment, and measure silent-failure risk versus extra bytes/latency against a larger initial subset. Still gated after v0.7: no causal selector passes the frozen development screen.

milestones.title: Later - Generalization and representation studies
milestones.description: After earlier gates, repeat on a 7B-class model and another family, then independently study quantization, group heterogeneity, lookahead, low-rank residuals, block-structured training, and verified storage paging.

issues.title: Deliver the reference apparatus and preserve the BF16 numerical failure
issues.body: Build paired SwiGLU packing and fail-closed numerical gates with immutable raw receipts. Completed: all 84 BF16 local checks pass, but 12/18 full-layout checks fail; sparsity is blocked. Separate FP32 control passes and completes 18 configurations. Validation: 22 tests at delivery and source/receipt hash checks. This closes the apparatus task, not a practical BF16 execution policy. Evidence: docs/protocol.md, docs/initial-results.md, results/initial-20260911, docs/releases/v0.1.0.md.

issues.title: Compare calibration-only co-activation packing with native, random, and popularity layouts
issues.body: Completed the declared WikiText pilot: 20,480 calibration tokens and 4,080 next-token predictions across 16 development articles. All correctness gates pass and 24 configurations complete. The tested co-activation heuristic loses to popularity in all four grouped settings; width-32/75% KL difference is +0.02524 with exploratory paired interval [+0.01648,+0.03468]. All 31 tests pass. Preserve this negative result; do not treat completion as the stage's cache/transfer gate. Evidence: docs/packing-pilot-results.md and docs/releases/v0.2.0.md.

issues.title: Isolate BF16 permutation sensitivity with explicit arithmetic controls
issues.body: Compare five arithmetic policies on the six smoke documents under the original tolerances. Completed: original-order down projection is exactly equal to BF16; reduced-precision reduction disabled and FP32 temporary policies still fail. Repeat with saved token/permutation receipts reproduces all 60 raw rows. Inverse gathers are diagnostic and have no performance claim. A deployable BF16 policy remains a separate open task. Evidence: docs/packing-pilot-results.md and results/packing-pilot-20260911/precision-receipted.

issues.title: Establish a practical BF16 grouped execution policy without relaxing numerical gates
issues.body: The canonical-order diagnostic is exact but materializes inverse gathers. Define and measure an execution policy that satisfies the original all-weight gates while supporting group-local execution. Charge precision conversion and temporary allocations; preserve original failures and compare all six documents plus a larger sample. Exit: passing function checks and explicit cost evidence, not a relaxed tolerance.

issues.title: Validate PyTorch 2.12 CUDA as a separate environment control
issues.body: Completed the isolated Python 3.14.3 torch/torchvision environment pair: 2.10.0/0.25.0 versus 2.12.0/0.27.0, CUDA 13.0, with every other effective package version aligned. Both full suites pass 59 tests. The 2.10 repeat reproduces all 60 archived arithmetic rows exactly; 2.12 still fails four of five policies under original numerical limits. Canonical down order is exact within each environment. Ordinary dense BF16 outputs differ across all six documents: L2 0.015831-0.024369, KL 0.001018-0.001567, top-1 agreement 95.51-98.78%. Complete inventories, pinned inputs, source snapshots, original failure receipts and manifest-bound logits are preserved. Initial shared torchvision was incompatible and the matching companion resolved it; this is not an unqualified torch-only attribution. This closes the environment-control experiment, not practical BF16 grouping. Evidence: docs/torch212-protocol.md, docs/torch212-results.md, results/torch-control-20260911, docs/releases/v0.5.0.md. Optional shared torchaudio retains a torch-2.10 dependency and is outside the validated text-model path.

issues.title: Add the original plan's ReLU positive control
issues.body: Completed the pinned OPT-1.3B FP32 ReLU control: 80 calibration / 16 development articles, 19,054 calibration tokens and 3,828 scored predictions. All 72 local plus 48 full-layout checks and all 192 exact-zero checks pass under original limits. About 96.04% of neurons are exactly zero; popularity exact-zero selection requires 19.80/40.10/60.40% of FFN bytes at widths 8/32/128. Fixed 75% width-128 popularity retention has relative PPL 1.014112 versus native 1.074781. Preserve all 545 raw rows, 24 aggregates, biased-projection accounting, immutable source and inputs, and the first incomplete-checkpoint failure. No transfer, bounded residency, runtime or SwiGLU generalization claim. Validation: 89 tests and independent ledger/aggregate validation. Evidence: docs/relu-control-protocol.md, docs/relu-control-results.md, results/relu-control-20260911, docs/releases/v0.6.0.md.

issues.title: Measure per-layer omission sensitivity and joint-layer interaction
issues.body: Completed the predeclared 66-condition per-layer and fixed-block study on all 28 FFNs, reusing frozen popularity/co-activation layouts and the 16 development articles. All 88 correctness checks pass; 1,056 document measurements are preserved. Top-four layers account for 20.82% / 19.57% of single-layer KL sums, and all 32 joint-layer document controls reproduce the parent quality metrics exactly. Co-activation improves single-layer KL in four layers; the complete curves preserve those exceptions and the lower-PPL/higher-KL middle-block result. Validation: 38 tests, reviewed provenance/interruption/plot checks, full raw-aggregate and weight-accounting verification. This closes the bounded experiment, not Stage 1 held-out quality. Evidence: docs/layer-study-protocol.md, docs/layer-study-results.md, results/layer-study-20260911, docs/releases/v0.3.0.md.

issues.title: Establish whole-document multi-domain held-out quality gates
issues.body: Build separate calibration/development/final-test document sets across code, arithmetic, copying, instructions, multilingual text, and topic switches. Declare task and perplexity tolerances before final scoring. Include per-layer and joint omissions, confidence intervals, and task outcomes; do not replace failed rows or retune against final test. Current Wikipedia pilot is development evidence only.

issues.title: Measure transfer amplification and bounded-cache traces at realistic group sizes
issues.body: Completed all 72 declared layout/width/retention conditions, 1,152 applied-mask traces, 36,864 document replay rows and 2,304 aggregates. Original numerical gates pass and 256 overlapping parent quality rows reproduce exactly. Only popularity/width 8/90% retention passes the prospective development screen: relative PPL 1.008978 and best simulated warm saving 15.54% with the 2 GiB equal-layer static cache. Nine of 16 documents individually exceed 1% PPL increase. LRU has zero hits under the validated distinct-other-layer bound; cold static preload and incoming reserve are charged. Full trace payloads are a hashed release asset. This completes the bounded trace experiment, not held-out quality or actual transfer/runtime gates. The frozen ordering nominates this condition for causal prediction. Evidence: docs/cache-trace-protocol.md, docs/cache-trace-results.md, results/cache-trace-20260911, docs/releases/v0.4.0.md.

issues.title: Compare causally available working-set predictors and their charged cost
issues.body:
Compare static popularity, last-token/window reuse, EMA and learned selectors with explicit feature availability, charged predictor storage and execution cost, independent omission audits, and approximate closed-loop evaluation. Measure quality/bytes/cost curves and topic transitions. Gate: useful proximity to hindsight at an affordable measured cost.

The first frozen-point experiment is complete in #15 / [v0.7.0](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/releases/tag/v0.7.0). All four causal selectors fail quality at Qwen popularity/width 8/90% retention: aggregate relative PPL 1.089204-1.158203 versus <=1.01, and all 16 articles individually fail for each selector. All pass the >=10% simulated warm-traffic screen; recency/EMA/learned also fail the <=10% CUDA-and-wall cost screen at about 72-83%. Static is cheap but loses quality. Incremental hindsight reaches 1.009318 and is ineligible. The complete raw ledger, masks, transition, generation and timing evidence are published.

This issue remains open for the broader useful-predictor gate and curves. No selector is nominated for paging/refinement. The negative result applies to these initial eager implementations and one operating point; it is not a proof that all predictors fail. Faster execution alone does not change the measured mask quality. Any new predictor, retention sweep or scale control needs a separate prospective protocol with fresh immutable receipts. Preserve this failed experiment and the original thresholds; do not retune on final test. Held-out quality #8 and runtime/refinement #11/#12 retain their separate gates.

issues.title: Implement bounded FFN residency with measured RAM-to-VRAM traffic
issues.body:
After prediction feasibility, implement CPU-backed groups, bounded pinned staging, bounded GPU slots, and kernels that avoid the claimed weight reads and work. Run dense reference separately without retaining a full GPU copy. Compare dense streaming, static/recency/activation-aware caches, and CPU execution alternatives at identical budgets. Charge scheduling, packing, transfers, synchronization, KV, and workspaces. Gate: measured end-to-end improvement over the strongest same-budget baseline.

Current gate status after v0.7.0 / #15: no causal selector qualifies at the frozen Qwen operating point. This phase remains unstarted and gated; completing the negative selector experiment does not satisfy prediction feasibility. Broader predictor issue #10 remains open.

issues.title: Test omission detection and additive refinement against larger initial subsets
issues.body:
Define unsafe omission before scoring. Estimate omitted effects from cheap causally available signals, preserve the FFN input, add missing group contributions before downstream commitment, and provide a bounded dense fallback. Plot silent quality failures against added bytes and latency, including detector cost. Residency misses and silent selection errors must remain separate. Gate: refinement improves the risk/cost frontier over simply selecting more initially; otherwise remove it.

Current gate status after v0.7.0 / #15: no causal selector qualifies at the frozen Qwen operating point. This phase remains unstarted and gated; completing the negative selector experiment does not satisfy prediction feasibility. Broader predictor issue #10 remains open.

issues.title: Replicate useful results on a larger model and another architecture
issues.body: After a useful small-model frontier, run a pinned 7B-class dense model and a second family such as Granite or LFM2. Validate real pretrained adapters and preserve architecture-specific normalization/mixing. Compare practical utility with optimized quantized resident models and smaller models at comparable quality/memory. A small-model negative result may justify a limited scale control; it does not justify an unrestricted runtime build.

issues.title: Evaluate quantization, residual representations, and storage paging as separate branches
issues.body: Keep quantization metadata aligned with neuron permutations and revalidate the function. Study heterogeneous groups, limited lookahead, low-rank-plus-residual decomposition, or training for block structure one change at a time; do not assume residuals are sparse or cheap. For NVMe/SSD work verify actual device reads, RAM cache residency, and swap. MTP integration, Bayesian state, and an always-on service remain deferred until core gates justify them.

issues.title: Deliver the first causal selector experiment at the frozen Qwen operating point
issues.body:
Completed the first causal selector experiment at the unchanged v0.4 Qwen popularity/width-8/90% condition and 2 GiB equal-layer static cache. None of the four causal selectors passes the frozen screen. Static, recency, EMA and learned relative PPL are 1.158203, 1.117159, 1.111589 and 1.089204; every causal selector exceeds 1% on all 16 development articles. All meet the simulated warm traffic screen (15.103-18.663% saving). Static costs 0.450% CUDA / 0.456% wall of paired resident dense FFNs; recency, EMA and learned cost about 72-83%, above the 10% affordability screen. Incremental hindsight reaches relative PPL 1.009318 and 15.539% warm saving, but is noncausal and cannot qualify.

The protocol/apparatus were pushed as [85efbc7](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/commit/85efbc771b75487b7aecfe0c521c1d3e4fd5452e) before fitting/evaluation. All 28 local plus 17 incremental layout gates pass under original 0.01 relative-L2 / 0.001 KL limits. Retain 307 raw rows, 85 document masks/audits, 20 generated-path traces, four dense continuations, 17 dense reference episodes, calibration statistics and fitted weights. All modes complete every article, the fixed topic transition and four closed-loop continuations. Persistent selector tensors reduce simulated FFN-cache capacity; query and necessary update cost are measured separately from the dense diagnostic.

Validation: 111 tests in both baseline torch 2.10 and separate torch 2.12 environments. The independent analyzer checks provenance, complete grids and ordering, numerical gates, actual reference NLL, charged mask replay, timing medians, generation receipts and every aggregate. Restoring all 124 payloads from three hashed release assets reproduces the validated analysis exactly.

This closes a bounded experiment, not the Stage 3 milestone or broader useful-predictor goal #10. Held-out quality #8 stays open. Physical paging #11 and refinement #12 remain gated. No physical transfer, bounded residency, task accuracy or speedup claim; full model and restoration copies remain resident. Predictor initialization traffic/time are excluded from replay, and the cost result covers the measured eager implementations. No final-test score or threshold/retention retuning follows from the failure.

Evidence: [v0.7.0 release](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/releases/tag/v0.7.0), [complete findings](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.7.0/docs/causal-control-results.md), [protocol](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.7.0/docs/causal-control-protocol.md), [archive and restoration](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/tree/v0.7.0/results/causal-control-20260911).
